posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked:
You need to use Windows Powershell with administrator permission. The regular one may not work with ssh-keygen. The prompt should be “PS C:\Windows\system32>” if you are in admin mode.

Use Windows search > type “Powershell” > At the side you will see “Run as administrator” > Click on it > If a prompt appears click “Yes” > run the command ssh-keygen

If the above doesn’t work then it means your Windows doesn’t have OpenSSH Client

To install OpenSSH client manually:

Open Settings, select System, then select Optional Features (also referred to as Manage optional features).

Then at the side of “Add an optional features” → View features

image846×152 4.3 KB

Type “OpenSSH” → Check the box → Click “Next” → Install

image668×923 6.79 KB

Or in admin mode of powershell run
Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Client~~~~0.0.1.0

After installation, restart your terminal and run: ssh-keygen
